entries.title: The prophet's lips and the Gospel
entries.en: Before the Gospel, the minister asks God to cleanse his heart and lips, recalling how a burning coal from the altar purified the prophet Isaiah. The prayer joins the holiness of the word proclaimed to the need for purity in the one who announces it.
entries.fr: Avant l’Évangile, le ministre demande à Dieu de purifier son cœur et ses lèvres, comme le charbon ardent pris sur l’autel purifia celles du prophète Isaïe. La sainteté de la parole proclamée appelle aussi la pureté de celui qui l’annonce.
entries.note: Do not force identical speaker/minister assignment across Low, Missa Cantata and Solemn forms. This is Scriptural prayer meaning, not a prescribed action.

source.work: D. I. Lanslots (1897), Illustrated Explanation of the Prayers and Ceremonies of the Mass

entries.title: The ascent of incense and the ascent of prayer
entries.en: As incense rises, the Church adopts the Psalmist's supplication that prayer rise before God like incense. The following verses ask for a guard over the lips and a heart not inclined to evil. The fragrant offering is therefore inseparable from the interior conversion for which the prayer asks.
entries.fr: Lorsque l’encens s’élève, l’Église reprend la supplication du psalmiste : que sa prière monte devant Dieu comme l’encens. Les versets suivants demandent de garder les lèvres et de préserver le cœur du mal. Le parfum offert renvoie donc à la conversion intérieure implorée par cette prière.
entries.note: Only where 1962 form permits this incensation. Do not infer scriptural symbolism as historical origin of incensing.

source.work: D. I. Lanslots (1897), Illustrated Explanation of the Prayers and Ceremonies of the Mass

entries.title: Sanctus and heavenly adoration
entries.en: The threefold Sanctus echoes both the seraphim's praise in Isaiah's vision and the unceasing adoration before God's throne in the Apocalypse. At the threshold of the Canon, earthly worship takes up the biblical language of the heavenly liturgy.
entries.fr: Le triple Sanctus reprend la louange des séraphins dans la vision d’Isaïe et l’adoration incessante devant le trône de Dieu dans l’Apocalypse. Au seuil du Canon, la liturgie terrestre emprunte les paroles de la louange céleste.
entries.note: This is one shared explanation for two biblical witnesses and one cue, never two separate duplicated Guides.

source.work: D. I. Lanslots (1897), Illustrated Explanation of the Prayers and Ceremonies of the Mass

entries.title: Benedictus and the welcome of Christ
entries.en: The Benedictus repeats the biblical acclamation greeting Jesus as he entered Jerusalem: blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. In the Mass these words acclaim the coming Lord; their use is not a second historical entry into Jerusalem.
entries.fr: Le Benedictus reprend l’acclamation qui accueillit Jésus lors de son entrée à Jérusalem : béni soit celui qui vient au nom du Seigneur. Dans la Messe, ces paroles acclament le Seigneur qui vient; elles ne décrivent pas une seconde entrée historique à Jérusalem.
entries.note: Matthew 21:9 is printed in checked Lanslots OCR; Mark 11:9-10 is merely an independent Gospel parallel and must not be attributed as his printed citation.

source.work: D. I. Lanslots (1897), Illustrated Explanation of the Prayers and Ceremonies of the Mass

entries.title: The chalice of salvation before priestly Communion
entries.en: Before receiving the Precious Blood, the celebrant makes his own the Psalmist's thanksgiving: what shall I render to the Lord for his gifts? He takes the chalice of salvation and invokes the Lord's name. This belongs to the priest's Communion, not to the earlier Offertory preparation of the chalice.
entries.fr: Avant de communier au Précieux Sang, le célébrant fait sienne l’action de grâces du psalmiste : que rendrai-je au Seigneur pour ses bienfaits ? Il prend le calice du salut et invoque le nom du Seigneur. Cette prière appartient à la Communion du prêtre, non à la préparation du calice à l’Offertoire.
entries.note: Psalm numbering follows Vulgate / Douay-Rheims here. Exact temporal location is sung source B075 / C0233.

source.work: D. I. Lanslots (1897), Illustrated Explanation of the Prayers and Ceremonies of the Mass

entries.title: The one bread and the unity of the Church
entries.en: Saint Paul links the one Eucharistic bread to the unity of those who partake of it: many persons become one body. The offering of bread can help the faithful contemplate this unity, but the explanation is theological context, not an additional prayer or gesture prescribed during the Offertory.
entries.fr: Saint Paul rattache l’unique pain eucharistique à l’unité de ceux qui y participent : plusieurs personnes forment un seul corps. L’offrande du pain invite à méditer cette unité; elle n’ajoute cependant ni prière ni geste prescrit aux cérémonies de l’Offertoire.
entries.note: Formation/topic context only; do not automatically attach to a live Offertory cue because the relevant verse's exact wording is absent from the 1962 prayer.

source.work: D. I. Lanslots (1897), Illustrated Explanation of the Prayers and Ceremonies of the Mass

entries.title: The martyrs beneath the heavenly altar
entries.en: Saint John's vision places the souls of those killed for God's word beneath the heavenly altar. This passage sheds devotional light on the honour paid to martyrs and their relics near the altar. It does not establish, by itself, when the Church's practice of placing relics in altars began.
entries.fr: Dans la vision de saint Jean, les âmes de ceux qui ont été mis à mort pour la parole de Dieu se trouvent sous l’autel céleste. Ce passage éclaire le respect porté aux martyrs et à leurs reliques près de l’autel, sans établir à lui seul l’origine historique de cette pratique.
entries.note: Historical/devotional introduction only; existing Oramus te uses reliquiae, but original Revelation words are not recited in that prayer.
